title: Queues and asynchronous work
goals: Explain the mechanism and terminology of queues and asynchronous work
Apply the stated procedure to a new case with a traceable result
Identify an assumption or limitation and design a revealing follow-up
vocabulary: A store of work awaiting processing
Receiving a previously delivered job again

blocks.text: Worker commits job J then crashes before queue acknowledgement. J is delivered again.
Consult durable job status; return committed result and acknowledge without repeating the effect. Delivery count is not effect count.

guided_practice.title: Trace the worked case

guided_practice.answer: Teacher explanation: Consult durable job status; return committed result and acknowledge without repeating the effect. Delivery count is not effect count.

independent_case.title: Apply a new case independently
independent_case.task: Jobs A, B, C accepted; A completed, B failed, C pending. How many completed, and may success be claimed for all accepted?
independent_case.answer: Teacher explanation: One complete, one failed, one pending. Acceptance is not completion; report each state.
independent_case.source: primary source W4, first curriculum occurrence

misconceptions: The worked result establishes every future case
Queue ordering and exactly-once properties must be declared, not assumed from a simple mock.
A missing input may be replaced without recording the change
A replacement changes the evidence or contract. Record the change and its justification; do not silently turn unknown into a measured value.
Repeating an assessed case is new independent evidence
A replay checks consistency. An example used for feedback or revision cannot later be described as untouched final evaluation.

blocks.text: A queued job is pending, running, completed or failed. Acknowledge only after the declared durable completion step. A repeated completed ID returns its prior result; unknown status needs reconciliation.
